summary: Norway is in the Schengen Area through its association agreement with the EU: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities including the US and UK get 90 days in any 180-day period counted across the whole Schengen Area, and everyone else needs a Schengen visa. Canada's travel advice says Svalbard, though Norwegian territory, is not part of the Schengen Area.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says Svalbard, although Norwegian territory, is not part of the Schengen area: you need a valid passport to enter it and must meet Schengen entry rules again when returning to mainland Norway.

Under Norway's Alcohol Act, drinks over 4.7% alcohol are sold in shops only by the state-owned Vinmonopolet, whose shops may sell from 08:30 to 18:00 (10:00 to 16:00 on the day before a Sunday or public holiday). Other shops may sell drinks of up to 4.7% from 08:00 to 18:00, and until 15:00 on the day before a Sunday or public holiday, unless the municipality sets other hours.

Canada's travel advice says Norway is prone to severe weather and its climate can be unpredictable at any time of year; it advises monitoring weather reports closely and warns of avalanche risk in mountain regions after heavy snowfall.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Norway?
faq.answer: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens don't need a visa at all. Citizens of around 60 visa-waiver countries — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan — can visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area. All other nationalities need a Schengen short-stay visa applied for through the Norwegian mission or visa center serving their place of residence.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Svalbard?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says Svalbard is Norwegian territory but not part of the Schengen area. You need a valid passport to enter it, and you must meet Schengen entry rules when you return to mainland Norway.

faq.question: Does time in Norway count toward the Schengen 90/180-day limit?
faq.answer: Yes. Norway is not in the EU, but it applies Schengen rules fully as an associated Schengen state — days spent in Norway are counted together with days in France, Germany and the rest of the Schengen Area.

faq.question: How long can UK citizens stay in Norway?
faq.answer: UK passport holders can visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, shared with the rest of the Schengen Area. The passport must have been issued within the last 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months beyond departure.

faq.question: Do I need ETIAS to visit Norway?
faq.answer: Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, visa-exempt travellers will need the authorisation (€20, valid 3 years) for Norway as for the rest of the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The official EU site is travel-europe.europa.eu.
